To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we present an accurate method for measuring Y_(SZ) from SZ observations, we show that Y_(SZ), measured within the SPT beam radius, is an excellent observable for cluster mass calibration, and we demonstrate this using a sample of galaxy cluster mass estimates derived from X-ray observations.

we have measured the integrated Compton parameter Y_(SZ) of a sample of galaxy cluster from the SPT survey and that Y_(SZ), measured within a radius of 0.3Mpc, has a log-normal scatter of about 25% with mass.
Y_(SZ), measured within an aperture of radius 0.3Mpc, has 26% ±9% intrinsic scatter with cluster mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of Y_(SZ) in the SPT data, and the use of this quantity as a mass proxy.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Y_(SZ), as measured in an aperture comparable to SPT beam size, is the SPT observable that is the most strongly correlated with cluster mass, and that this is true in both simulated observations of an SZ survey and in the real data.

the Y_SZ measured within an angular aperture comparable in size to the SPT-Sz beam size is the SPT-Sze observable with the lowest intrinsic scatter with mass, and is equivalent, in this sense, to the SPT cluster detection signal.
we have shown that Y_(SZ), measured within a radius that is comparable to the SPC beam size, is the SPT observable that best constrains the mass scaling relation for galaxy clusters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SPT-SZE selected cluster sample has a scatter in mass of 20% and a scatter in Y_(SZ, 0.'75) of 21%.

the SZ effect, measured in multiple frequency bands, is a robust observable for measuring cluster integrated Comptonization, and that Y_(SZ), measured in a small angular aperture, has a lower scatter with mass than any other SZ-derived observable.

the SPT observable with the lowest scatter with cluster mass is cluster detection significance, but that Y_(SZ), measured within an aperture of radius comparable to the S PT beam size, is equivalent to SPT cluster significance for scatter with mass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SZ effect is an excellent mass proxy for SPT clusters.

Y_(SZ)-based mass estimates are now competitive with X-ray-based mass estimates, and that the combination of Y_(SZ) measurements and X-ray-based mass measurements will be useful in constraining cosmological models and the mass scaling relations for clusters of galaxies.

the SPT-Sz survey is a very powerful tool to measure the integrated Compton-y parameter of galaxy clusters and that Y_(SZ), measured within an angular aperture comparable in size to the SPT primary beam, is a good proxy for cluster mass.
